Commentary.Commentary: The match officials are out in the middle followed by the Netherlands players who take their respective positions in the field. Kashyap Prajapati and Jatinder Singh are the two openers for Oman while Logan van Beek will bowl the first over. Let's go...
...RUN CHASE...
The conditions are still overcast and there should be some movement for the Dutch bowlers here. The Oman openers will need to be a bit careful here.

The Oman bowlers bowled their hearts out but they were not backed well in the field and have given away at the least 30-35 runs in the field. Mohammad Nadeem was good with the ball as he picked up a couple but was under-bowled. Bilal Khan picked up 3 wickets and Ayaan Khan and Fayyaz Butt were amongst the wicket-takers as they took a wicket each too. They have left a massive task for their batters to accomplish though and Netherlands have a decent bowling unit to defend this target. Can Oman chase it down to spoil the party mood in Amsterdam or will the Dutch inflict a heavy defeat on the Associate nation and jump above Scotland in the points table? Do join use shortly for the run chase.

Vikramjit Singh is up for a chat. He says that it feels good to get his first century as it took 20 innings to get but it is finally here. Adds that he and Max O'Dowd complement each other well as they communicate well and are having fun. Mentions that he was just trying to use his feet against the pacers and it worked out well as he was able to find the boundaries.

The Dutch innings started off a bit cautiously as both openers were watchful to start off but a rain delay awakened something and Vikramjit Singh came out with a positive mindset to take the attack to the opposition. The openers put up a 117-run partnership to put them in a commanding position and lay a perfect platform for their hitters to take control of the game towards the end. Vikramjit was sensational with his shot selection and strokeplay as he smashed the Oman bowlers all over the park for his maiden ODI century as he scored 110 before perishing. Wesley Barresi played a sensational knock as he smoked the Oman bowlers all over the park with a strike of over 145 scoring 97 but missed out on his century. Handy cameos from Max O'Dowd, Bas de Leede, and Saqib Zulfiqar helped them post a mammoth total.

In a must-win game, the Dutch side has put on an outstanding batting effort having scored 362 runs for the loss of 7 wickets in their quota of 48 overs! They had contributions through the batting line-up and a special note has to be taken about the way they accumulated the runs with some good running between the wicket in the middle of all the boundaries they accumulated. Oman had a bowling performance to forget and will need to do something special here to get over the finish line.

Netherlands' inning comes to an end on 362 runs and this has been a dominating batting display by the lads in orange.

Oman on the contrary has had an upside-down tournament where they won the first two games and then are on a losing spree of 3 on a trot. The defeat against Zimbabwe came at a cost as skipper Zeeshan Maqsood injured himself and Oman were knocked out of the qualification scenarios. The graph of the bowlers and the batter has dipped massively in the recent games as they have conceded in excess of 300 in the last two games and were bundled out under 100 in the other game. The batters need to step up big time and the bowlers are crying for backing from the fielders as the fielding has been really poor from the Associate side. Can Oman knock the Dutch out of the qualification scenario or will the Dutch stay in the hunt for the last spot up for grabs? Let's see as toss and team updates coming soon...

Netherlands have had an amazing outing in Zimbabwe as they have played an aggressive brand of cricket with clinical performances and the best of them came against the mighty West Indies where they chased down a mammoth score of 374.
